reason: contract_loader.py was changed to validate contract_surface_lock.surface_sha256 when present, while preserving fail-closed loading for required schemas, registries, boundary docs, malformed manifests, and legacy git-SHA locks.
user_intent_alignment_summary: The user required Exception Lake to consume pinned contracts and evidence without owning canonical meaning. Surface-lock validation keeps Exception Lake as a consumer and removes recursive drift from non-authority Substrate changes.
diff_review_summary: The loader continues to load the export manifest first, falls back only where already allowed, validates required schema/doc paths, and rejects malformed locks. The replacement adds contract surface hash validation and returns validated_ref_type=contract_surface_sha256 for surface locks. It does not grant Exception Lake canonical schema, routing, lifecycle, promotion, or AI front-door authority.
why_merge_not_sufficient: The old git-SHA-only validation path could not express the new contract boundary. A direct extension was needed so surface locks and legacy locks fail closed through a single loader contract.
replacement_justification: The new loader behavior is necessary for consumers to validate the registry-defined contract authority surface instead of every Substrate commit. This prevents managed-patch decisions, reports, docs, scripts, tests, and audit artifacts from forcing consumer lock drift unless the contract-surface registry includes them.
alternatives_considered: Keep Exception Lake on whole-commit validation. Rejected because it preserves lock recursion.
Let Exception Lake define its own contract-surface registry. Rejected because Semantic Substrate owns canonical contract authority.
removed_content_summary: Archive or git SHA validation as the only accepted runtime reference
source_refs: Codex FAIL blocker: consumer lock provenance mismatch
